**Video:** [Lec 38 — Dual Function in SVM](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RXzcClx44Tw)

## Learning goals

- Construct the **dual function** by minimizing the Lagrangian over $(w,b)$.
- State the dual QP in the multipliers $\mu$.
- Define **support vectors** and recover $w^\star$ from them.

## Before this clicks

Lagrangian for hard-margin SVM (multipliers $\mu_i\ge 0$):

$$
\mathcal{L}(w,b,\mu)
=\frac12\|w\|^2
-\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mu_i\Big(y_i(w^\top x_i+b)-1\Big).
$$

Dual function: $Q(\mu)=\inf_{w,b}\mathcal{L}(w,b,\mu)$. Dual problem: maximize $Q(\mu)$ over $\mu\ge 0$ (with feasibility constraints that keep $Q$ finite).

---

## Main ideas

### 1. Stationarity in $w$ and $b$

Minimizing $\mathcal{L}$ w.r.t. $w$ yields

$$
w=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mu_i y_i x_i.
$$

Minimizing w.r.t. $b$ forces the constraint

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mu_i y_i=0
$$

(otherwise $\inf_b\mathcal{L}=-\infty$).

### 2. Dual problem (schematic)

Substitute $w(\mu)$ back to get a concave quadratic in $\mu$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\max_{\mu}\quad &
\sum_i\mu_i
-\frac12\sum_{i,j}\mu_i\mu_j y_i y_j\,x_i^\top x_j\\
\text{s.t.}\quad &
\mu_i\ge 0,\qquad
\sum_i\mu_i y_i=0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Solved with standard QP / SMO-style solvers $\Rightarrow\mu^\star$.

### 3. Support vectors

**Support vectors** are training points with $\mu_i^\star>0$. Geometrically they lie on the margin hyperplanes. Points with $\mu_i^\star=0$ can be removed without changing $w^\star$.

Optimal boundary:

$$
w^\star=\sum_{i\in\mathrm{SV}}\mu_i^\star y_i x_i,
$$

a linear combination of support vectors only. Bias $b^\star$ is recovered from any margin SV using $y_i(w^{\star\top}x_i+b^\star)=1$.

### 4. What’s next

1. Data **not** linearly separable $\to$ slack variables (soft margin).
2. Nonlinear boundaries $\to$ feature maps / **kernels**.

---

## Worked mini-example

If only two opposite-label points are SVs with equal $\mu>0$ satisfying $\sum\mu_i y_i=0$, then $w$ is parallel to the difference of those two feature vectors — the boundary sits between them, as geometry demands.

---

## Common confusions

| Confusion | Clarification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Every training point is a support vector | Only those with $\mu_i>0$. |
| Dual ignores $b$ | $b$ is recovered after $\mu^\star$; the $\sum\mu_i y_i=0$ constraint comes from optimizing $b$. |
| Need all $x_i$ at test time | Decision uses SVs only (still may be many). |

## Self-check questions

1. Write $w$ in terms of $\mu_i,y_i,x_i$ at the Lagrangian minimum.
2. Why require $\sum_i\mu_i y_i=0$?
3. Define a support vector via $\mu_i$.
4. Write the dual objective’s quadratic term involving $x_i^\top x_j$.
5. How do you recover $b^\star$?
